executive_summary: Today's intelligence picture is defined by two converging mega-trends: the accelerating weaponization of artificial intelligence across both offensive and defensive cyber operations, and the compounding strain on U.S. military readiness and fiscal capacity at a moment of rising great-power competition. On the cyber and OT front, AI is no longer a theoretical threat multiplier — Chinese actors are actively deploying AI-assisted malware in live espionage campaigns against government targets, adversaries are using AI-generated scripts to attack critical industrial control systems, and even trusted security tools like Microsoft Defender are being subverted as attack vectors, suggesting the defensive perimeter is eroding faster than institutions can adapt. The military thread compounds this concern: the Iran war is exposing chronic Navy tempo problems and crowding out funding for next-generation programs like Golden Dome, while the Army is shutting down drone experimentation in Europe just as China conducts naval provocations near Japan and integrates AI into PLA command structures over internal resistance, signaling Beijing is making long-term bets on military-AI integration that Washington is currently too resource-constrained to match. The connective tissue across all four sections is that the U.S. faces simultaneous fiscal, operational, and technological stress precisely when adversaries — particularly China — are making coordinated advances in AI-enabled military and intelligence capabilities, and the risk is that these pressures are not being assessed together at the strategic

sections.title: Cyber
sections.intro: Today's cyber landscape is dominated by sophisticated kernel-level attack techniques, AI-assisted espionage, and a newly identified Chinese threat actor pushing the boundaries of post-compromise tooling.

items.headline: Check Point reveals how Microsoft's own Defender driver can be turned into a kernel-level attack tool
items.summary: Check Point Research has disclosed a technique dubbed 'BTR Reforged' that weaponizes a signed Microsoft remediation driver to execute arbitrary file and registry operations at Ring 0 — the highest privilege level — without exploits or memory corruption. Because the driver is trusted and signed by Microsoft, it bypasses most security controls and detection heuristics. This represents a significant advancement in Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) abuse and raises hard questions about the implicit trust placed in vendor-signed security components.

items.headline: Chinese threat actor UAT-10147 deploys AI-assisted, cross-platform SPECTRE implant with rootkit capabilities
items.summary: Cisco Talos has identified UAT-10147, a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group targeting vulnerable web servers globally, deploying a sophisticated implant called SPECTRE that combines cross-platform C2, process injection, credential theft, and kernel-level EDR bypass via BYOVD techniques. Separately, Talos also found the group integrating agentic AI into post-compromise operations, marking a notable escalation in automation sophistication for a criminal-tier actor. The combination of AI-assisted development and advanced evasion tooling suggests the operational gap between nation-state and cybercrime actors is narrowing rapidly.

items.headline: China's SilkParasite group uses AI-developed malware in Central Asian government espionage campaign
items.summary: Suspected Chinese military-affiliated hackers operating under the 'SilkParasite' moniker have been caught using AI-assisted malware development to target Central Asian government networks in an espionage campaign. The use of AI in malware construction signals a broader trend of state actors leveraging generative tools to accelerate development cycles and reduce tradecraft indicators. Central Asian governments, often under-resourced for cyber defense, present attractive targets for intelligence collection tied to regional geopolitical interests.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: CISA flags two actively exploited vulnerabilities including critical TrueConf authentication bypass
items.summary: CISA added two vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including CVE-2026-72529, a missing authentication flaw in TrueConf Server that allows unauthenticated access to critical functions. Active exploitation of video conferencing infrastructure is a recurring vector for initial access in both espionage and ransomware campaigns. Federal agencies face binding remediation deadlines, and private sector organizations using TrueConf should treat patching as urgent.

sections.title: Geopolitical
sections.intro: Strategic competition between major powers is intensifying across economic, technological, and territorial dimensions, with the U.S. facing simultaneous pressure points from China, Canada, and its own fiscal trajectory.

items.headline: Canada Racing to Seal Trade Deal Before New U.S. Tariffs Take Effect
items.summary: Senior Canadian officials are actively negotiating to avoid a fresh round of 50 percent U.S. tariffs on steel, aluminum, autos, and lumber. The deadline pressure signals a broader pattern of the Trump administration using tariff threats as leverage, with bilateral trade relations remaining structurally fragile. Watch whether Ottawa makes asymmetric concessions on auto supply chains or lumber quotas to secure a deal.

items.headline: Xi Pushes AI Command Integration Despite PLA Resistance to Replacing Human Judgment
items.summary: China's People's Liberation Army has publicly insisted that AI cannot replace battlefield commanders, even as Xi Jinping accelerates efforts to embed AI deeper into command-and-control systems. The tension exposes a civil-military friction point: institutional resistance from commanders wary of accountability gaps versus top-down pressure for faster decision cycles. This gap between doctrine and direction will shape how the PLA actually performs in a high-intensity conflict scenario.

items.headline: Sino-Russian Naval Drills Near Disputed Okinotori Rock Test Japan's Maritime Claims
items.summary: China and Russia conducted live-fire exercises within Japan's claimed exclusive economic zone around Okinotori, a feature Tokyo bases a 150,000-square-mile maritime claim on despite it being barely above water at high tide. China does not recognize Okinotori as an island capable of generating EEZ rights under UNCLOS, making these drills a deliberate legal and strategic challenge rather than a routine exercise. The episode illustrates how Beijing and Moscow are coordinating to erode the rules-based maritime order across the Pacific.

items.headline: U.S. Bond Market Stress Signals Deeper Structural Fiscal Risk
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is intervening to address rising bond yields, but analysts warn the underlying fiscal rot—driven by sustained deficit spending and ballooning national debt—is not addressable through market-stabilization tactics alone. Elevated yields increase borrowing costs across the economy and constrain the fiscal space needed to fund defense and strategic competition priorities. If confidence in U.S. fiscal discipline continues to erode, the geopolitical consequences for dollar dominance and alliance credibility are significant.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: The Iran war continues to expose systemic U.S. military readiness gaps while domestic political battles threaten next-generation defense programs.

items.headline: Iran war lays bare Navy's chronic operational tempo crisis
items.summary: Years of carrier availability shortfalls and unsustainable deployment cycles have been thrown into sharp relief by the demands of the Iran conflict. The strain raises serious questions about the Navy's ability to sustain high-intensity operations while managing global commitments. Watch for Congressional pressure on shipbuilding timelines and maintenance funding as after-action assessments circulate.

items.headline: Golden Dome missile shield faces funding squeeze as Iran war costs mount
items.summary: Rep. Jeff Crank, the caucus chair backing the national missile defense initiative, acknowledged that war spending is directly competing with Golden Dome's budget prospects. The admission signals that even politically popular defense programs are vulnerable when active-conflict costs dominate appropriations discussions. This is a key indicator of whether long-range strategic modernization will be deferred in favor of near-term operational demands.

items.headline: U.S. Army shutters experimental European drone battalion after single exercise cycle
items.summary: The Army's experimental drone unit in Europe will revert to its core airborne infantry mission following Exercise Saber Junction, ending a trial that was closely watched as a model for integrating unmanned systems into ground formations. The disbandment suggests the concept either failed to meet operational benchmarks or was deprioritized amid broader force structure pressures. The outcome will inform how the Army paces future drone integration experiments.

items.headline: Russian space activity warning forces U.S. Air Force C-17 to abort Antarctic mission
items.summary: A USAF C-17 departing New Zealand turned back after receiving a Russian-issued notice of potentially hazardous space activity along its flight path, an unusual incident that highlights the growing intersection of space domain operations and conventional military logistics. The episode underscores how orbital threats and debris events can directly disrupt real-world military missions. It will likely prompt review of contingency protocols for flights in contested or affected corridors.

sections.title: Intel / OSINT
sections.intro: Open-source analysis is surfacing infrastructure changes and capability developments that official channels have not disclosed, from border construction inside a national park to China's newest military airlifter.

items.headline: Satellite imagery reveals over five miles of new CBP road construction inside Big Bend National Park
items.summary: Bellingcat analyzed commercial satellite imagery to document active 'Smart Wall' infrastructure — roads, barriers, and sensors — being built inside a protected national park without public announcement. The find demonstrates how OSINT methods can surface federal activity that bypasses normal environmental review and public disclosure processes. Watch for similar analysis of other protected or sensitive federal lands where construction activity may be underway.

items.headline: Open-source imagery provides clearest view yet of China's Y-15 turboprop military transport
items.summary: New imagery of China's four-engine Y-15 airlifter offers the most detailed public look at a platform designed to modernize the PLA's tactical and strategic transport capabilities. The aircraft fills a gap between light utility helicopters and heavy jet airlifters, improving China's ability to project forces into austere or high-altitude environments. Analysts should track Y-15 basing patterns and production rates as indicators of PLA operational reach.

items.headline: General Atomics unveils Wildfire as its MQ-9 successor in Pentagon next-gen drone competition
items.summary: General Atomics has publicly entered the Wildfire concept into a DoD competition for a next-generation medium-altitude, long-endurance ISR and strike platform to replace the MQ-9 Reaper. The disclosure gives adversaries and analysts early insight into U.S. thinking about future uncrewed ISR architecture and performance thresholds. The competition outcome will shape American drone strike and surveillance capacity for the 2030s.

items.headline: Senators demand answers from TikTok on deliberate withholding of user safety features
items.summary: Bipartisan Senate pressure is mounting after evidence emerged that TikTok withheld safety protections from a subset of American users, raising questions about whether the decisions were algorithmically or policy-driven — and by whom. The letter from Blackburn and Blumenthal signals continued legislative focus on TikTok's data governance and the opacity of its content and safety decision-making. This adds another dimension to ongoing national security scrutiny of the platform's operational transparency.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: AI-enabled attack tooling against industrial control systems is emerging as the dominant threat theme, with U.S. agencies issuing urgent warnings about PLC exploitation while guidance bodies race to help under-resourced operators catch up.

items.headline: CISA, NSA, and FBI Warn of AI-Generated Scripts Being Used to Attack Siemens S7 PLCs
items.summary: A joint advisory from three U.S. agencies flags active threat activity targeting Siemens S7 Series PLCs, with adversaries using AI-generated scripts to manipulate industrial processes — a notable escalation in attacker capability against OT environments. The advisory signals that the barrier to conducting sophisticated ICS attacks is lowering as AI tooling becomes accessible to a broader range of threat actors. Asset owners running S7 PLCs in critical infrastructure should treat this as an urgent patching and network segmentation priority.

items.headline: Mass Compromise of 14,000 IP Cameras Across Ukraine and Russia Highlights OT-Adjacent Surveillance Risk
items.summary: Operation CameraSwarm targeted Dahua IP cameras at scale, focusing on Russian and CIS telecom network blocks in what appears to be a deliberate intelligence-gathering or disruption campaign. While IP cameras are not traditional OT devices, their widespread deployment at industrial and critical infrastructure sites makes mass compromise events like this directly relevant to physical security convergence risks. The campaign underscores the need to treat internet-exposed IoT and surveillance hardware as part of the OT attack surface.

items.headline: NIST Publishes Actionable OT Cybersecurity Guidance Targeting Building Automation Systems Operators
items.summary: NIST released a practical quick-start infographic specifically designed for resource-constrained Building Automation and Control Systems (BACS) operators, addressing a segment of the OT community that often lacks dedicated security staff or budgets. The guidance is timely given the escalating threat environment and fills a gap between high-level frameworks and the operational realities of smaller facility operators. Watch for whether this prompts broader adoption of baseline OT hygiene practices in sectors like healthcare, education, and commercial real estate.

items.headline: AI-Assisted Security Tool Deployed to Harden Viasat Satellite Network After Russian Cyberattack
items.summary: Atalanta's Argo platform is being used to continuously validate the resilience of Viasat's satellite communications network, which was crippled by a Russian cyberattack at the outset of the Ukraine war in February 2022. The deployment represents a real-world case study in applying AI-driven automated security validation to critical communications infrastructure — a category that sits at the intersection of OT, military, and civilian systems. The broader implication is that AI-assisted defense tools are beginning to reach operational maturity in high-stakes infrastructure environments.
